_comment: Design §4.4 authority baseline: sources in authority order. Two rules, checked both ways against the live registry by opendata/data/registry.py:reconcile_authority (guard tests/test_authority_reconciliation.py, audit docs/evidence/C23): a domain served by more than one source must be listed, and no row may name a source that registers no capability there. Single-source domains are deliberately not listed: there is nothing to order, and inventing a row would let the table certify a ranking it cannot express (the reason earlier rounds left fund_action and the overseas daily leg out - AC-10 called that 登记成权威序属口径造假). Three rows the table already carried (financial_indicator, instrument, trading_calendar) are kept with their one real entry because an earlier round wrote them; they state who serves the domain today, carry no ordering decision, and the guard will demand a genuine ordering the day a second source registers. C23 removed seven pairs that named legs which were never registered: the stock_adjust and futures_fundamentals rows went entirely (no capability registers either domain - stock_adjust factors are produced outside the routing layer, by the market-dumps channel a_share_adjustment_factors_event_none_all feeding ods and FactorBuilder deriving dwd_stock_adjust, see opendata_fuyao/endpoint_map.yaml market-dumps adjustment-factors; futures_fundamentals is client_only, 端外暂不开放), financial_indicator lost ths (the endpoint is available but deliberately not implemented: the response is data.abilities with no per-row disclosure date while the FinancialIndicator contract requires announce_date, measured in C10), and instrument / trading_calendar lost akshare (C13/C14 landed the ths producer side; akshare never registered a leg). GET /api/v1/data/sources renders this table, which is why a stale row is a public over-claim rather than a comment. Domestic domains: ths is authoritative, akshare the fallback. fund_etf_daily is the one reversed domestic pair: the ths leg answers only a rolling 1827 days (measured, docs/evidence/C20), so it cannot answer since-inception requests and akshare stays first. Macro domains are listed per measured substitutability: a row orders only the legs sharing one (period, market), because source=auto refuses to pick across markets (registry._reject_cross_market_auto). fred legs are unverified and key-required, so they never participate in auto and are not ranked - the guard demands a listing only for auto-eligible sources. economy_unemployment puts oecd before imf on the measured publication shape: with the window end pushed to 2031, imf returns 6 rows dated after the last completed year 2025 (WEO projections mixed into the same value field) while oecd returns none (docs/evidence/C22). Measured there too: the two legs agree for USA (0.097pp) and JPN (0.174pp) but not for DEU (0.421pp over the 0.3pp tolerance), so they are not value-swappable for every area - open finding, not a ranking question. economy_cpi keeps ecb first on a declared, not measured, basis: the 1M legs are not value-comparable (euro-area aggregate vs a UK series on the eu-labelled leg, means 2.394 and 0.223, max per-date gap 10.181), so no value-level judge exists and the euro-area publisher wins. economy_gdp and economy_rate have one verified leg per (period, market) - listed so the coverage guard cannot silently regress. Loaded by opendata/data/registry.py.
